title: Restriction-transpose resolution model for the specified comparison mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-size-convention], with their constant-$\Lambda$ module categories and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes, $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison inverse image, and $N_T=\nu_{T,*}$ for its right adjoint [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact].
Let $u:U\to V$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $F$ a $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $i:F[0]\to I$, $t:A_UI\to J$ quasi-isomorphisms with $I,J$ nonnegative, termwise injective K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Put $h=\operatorname{adj}(t):I\to N_UJ$, $C=u_{\mathrm{et},*}I$, and $D=u_{\mathrm{proet},*}J$, using the ordinary module direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $\delta:N_Vu_{\mathrm{proet},*}\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{\mathrm{et},*}N_U$ be the restriction identity: on each etale $W/V$ both sides evaluate a pro-etale sheaf $G$ as $G(W\times_VU)$, with its restriction maps and coefficient action. Set $k=\delta_J^{-1}\circ u_{\mathrm{et},*}(h):C\to N_VD$ and let $d:A_VC\to D$ be its adjunction transpose [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].
Then, under the canonical resolution identifications $QC\cong Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}F$ and $QD\cong Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_UF$ (the latter induced by $t\circ A_U(i)$), $Qd$ is the specified comparison $b_{u,F}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. More explicitly, writing $l=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ for the etale module inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $p=u_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$ and $\varepsilon^e,\varepsilon^p$ for their ordinary adjunction counits, and $a^0:A_Ul\xrightarrow{\sim}pA_V$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], one has the chain-map equality
$$\varepsilon^p_J\circ p(d)\circ a^0_C=t\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_I).$$
Consequently its derived transpose is exactly $A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,F})\circ a_{u,Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}F}^{-1}$ with the specified derived counit and pullback comparison. In every degree and for every terminal section $z$ of $C$, $k(z)=h(z)$ as a section of $J$ on $U$, and $d(A_V(z))=h(z)$. Here comparison pullback of a section uses the canonical constant-ring unit identification. No preservation of injective objects by $A_U$ or $A_V$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $r=u_{\mathrm{et},*}$ and $s=u_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ for the ordinary direct images, reserving $Rr,Rs$ for their derived functors. On an etale object $W/V$, both $N_VsG$ and $rN_UG$ are $G(W\times_VU)$. On an arrow $W'\to W$ both use restriction along $W'\times_VU\to W\times_VU$, and on coefficients both send a constant scalar to the same constant section. Thus the identity on these modules defines the natural, linear isomorphism $\delta:N_Vs\cong rN_U$ in the statement. These are identities of sheaf functors, so applying them termwise also gives an isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; sectionwise definition of restriction and direct image (agent calculation).

proof.text:
Use the composite adjunctions $A_Ul\dashv rN_U$ and $pA_V\dashv N_Vs$. Denote their Hom bijections by $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$, respectively. The canonical comparison $a^0:A_Ul\cong pA_V$ is the left-adjoint conjugate of the restriction identity $\delta$; this is the normalization of the canonical pullback comparison. Explicitly, for $g:pA_VM\to G$,
$$\Phi_1(g\circ a^0_M)=\delta_G\circ\Phi_2(g).$$
Indeed the conjugate unit equation gives $rN_U(a^0_M)\eta_{1,M}=\delta_{pA_VM}\eta_{2,M}$; compose with $rN_U(g)$ and use naturality of $\delta$. This proves the displayed Hom equation from the cited unit equation, rather than assuming compatibility of arbitrary isomorphisms. The termwise-adjunction theorem gives these same adjunctions on complexes, with the ordinary units and counits in each degree. All ensuing equalities hold as chain maps, before passage to homotopy or localization.

source.place: Tags 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, and 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits; derived.tex Tag 0FND, fourth Hom identification.

proof.text:
Let $\eta^A$ denote the comparison adjunction unit. Since $h=N_U(t)\eta^A_I$, the transpose of $t\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_I)$ under $A_U\dashv N_U$ is $h\circ\varepsilon^e_I$, by naturality of $\eta^A$. Its further transpose under $l\dashv r$ is
$$r(h)\circ r(\varepsilon^e_I)\circ\eta^e_{rI}=r(h),$$
by the triangle identity. On the other hand put $g=\varepsilon^p_J\circ p(d):pA_VC\to J$. Its $p\dashv s$ transpose is $d$ by the triangle identity, and its further comparison transpose is $N_V(d)\eta^A_C=k$. Step 2 therefore gives $\Phi_1(g a^0_C)=\delta_J k=r(h)=\Phi_1(t A_U(\varepsilon^e_I))$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection proves
$$\varepsilon^p_J\circ p(d)\circ a^0_C=t\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_I),$$
including every degree and differential. This uses precisely $k=\delta_J^{-1}r(h)$, so the direction of the restriction isomorphism is fixed.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; the composite Hom bijections and triangle identities, calculated for t and d.

proof.text:
Both $l$ and $p$ are exact module inverse images: use the etale module exactness theorem and the pro-etale operations with the constant-ring identification. The comparison functors $A_T$ are exact as well. Consequently their derived functors and pullback comparisons are represented termwise, so the derived comparison $a$ on $QC$ is $Q(a^0_C)$ under the exact-localization identifications. Set $j=t\circ A_U(i):A_UF[0]\to J$. Exactness of $A_U$ makes $A_U(i)$ a quasi-isomorphism; hence $j$ is one. The supplied K-injective $I,J$ compute the derived direct images. Denote the canonical resolution isomorphisms by
$$\rho_e:QC\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr(F),\qquad \rho_p:QD\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs(A_UF).$$
Their augmentations are respectively $i$ and $j$. Computation on any supplied K-injective, not just a prechosen replacement, follows from the K-injective computation theorem; its existence hypothesis is supplied by the ringed-site K-injective existence theorem on the small sites in the statement.

source.place: Tags 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor. Ringed-site existence: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A5, section-unbounded.

proof.text:
Apply the representative formula in the general pre-derived adjunction theorem, with the exact left adjoint computed without replacement. For the etale pair take the right resolution $i:F[0]\to I$, the left replacement $\mathrm{id}_C$, and the map $\mathrm{id}_C:C\to rI$. For the pro-etale pair take $j:A_UF[0]\to J$, the left replacement $\mathrm{id}_{A_VC}$, and the map $d:A_VC\to sJ$. It gives, under the exact-localization comparisons,
$$\varepsilon^e_F\circ l(\rho_e)=Q(i)^{-1}\circ Q(\varepsilon^e_I),$$
$$\operatorname{adj}_p(\rho_p\circ Qd)=Q(j)^{-1}\circ Q(\varepsilon^p_J\circ p(d)).$$
The cocones in that theorem are precisely the canonical derived-functor comparison followed by inverse derived image of the augmentation; Step 4 identifies them with $\rho_e,\rho_p$. Thus these formulas concern the specified derived adjunctions and their counits. They do not choose an unrelated adjunction on the same functors.

source.place: Tag 0FND, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, its colimit-of-Hom construction; Tags 0DVC and 09T5 for the resulting canonical adjunction.

proof.text:
Localize the equality of Step 3 and apply Step 5. Since $Qj=Q(t)\circ A_U(Qi)$, cancellation gives
$$\operatorname{adj}_p(\rho_p Qd)\circ Q(a^0_C)
 =Q(j)^{-1}Q(t)A_UQ(\varepsilon^e_I)
 =A_U(\varepsilon^e_F\circ l(\rho_e)).$$
Naturality of the specified comparison says
$$pA_V(\rho_e)\circ Q(a^0_C)=a_{u,RrF}\circ A_Ul(\rho_e).$$
Combine these equations and cancel the isomorphism $A_Ul(\rho_e)$ to obtain, for $B=\rho_p\circ Qd\circ A_V(\rho_e)^{-1}$,
$$\operatorname{adj}_p(B)\circ a_{u,RrF}=A_U(\varepsilon^e_F).$$
Hence $\operatorname{adj}_p(B)=A_U(\varepsilon^e_F)\circ a_{u,RrF}^{-1}=q_{u,F}$. The canonical-mate node defines $b_{u,F}$ to be the unique transpose of exactly this $q_{u,F}$. Thus $B=b_{u,F}$, which is the claimed identification of $Qd$ and the claimed derived-transpose formula.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; cancellation in the specified counit normalization (agent calculation).

proof.text: Fix a degree $n$ and $z\in C^n(V)=I^n(U)$. The restriction comparison $\delta$ at the terminal object is the identity, so $k^n_V(z)=h^n_U(z)\in J^n(U)$. The adjunction equation $N_V(d)\circ\eta^A_C=k$ evaluated on this same section gives $d^n(A_V(z))=k^n_V(z)=h^n_U(z)$. Here $A_V(z)$ denotes the section obtained by the comparison unit; the constant-ring unit identification is the one in the site-comparison module adjunction. These computations use no cocycle condition on $z$ and apply in every degree, proving the final clause.
